Started LedgerApplication in 7.84 seconds (process running for 8.61)
Last State:     Terminated
Reason:       OOMKilled
Exit Code:    137
Restart Count:  6
Limits:
memory:  1Gi

question: Why does ledger-svc keep restarting?
options: Heap leak in ledger-svc 4.12.0 filling up the Java heap
Node memory pressure evicting the pod to reclaim RAM
-Xmx1536m heap is larger than the 1Gi container limit
Netty direct buffers leaking off-heap past the limit

explanation.cause: The JVM’s max heap (1.5 GiB) was set above the container’s 1 GiB memory limit
explanation.why: An explicit -Xmx overrides the JVM’s container-aware heap sizing. G1 grows the heap lazily toward 1.5 GiB, so the cgroup hits 1 GiB first and the kernel OOM killer SIGKILLs the process (exit 137) before the JVM ever feels heap pressure — which is why no OutOfMemoryError is ever logged.
explanation.tell: OOMKilled / exit 137 with no OutOfMemoryError, a sawtooth that starts right after the 09:01 -Xmx change, and 1536m printed at startup against a 1Gi limit.

items.value: index loads before the HTTP server starts listening

question: Why can’t catalog-api 3.8.0 stay up?
options: Corrupt index snapshot crashing the loader partway through
Liveness probe kills pods before the index finishes loading
Pods OOMKilled while loading the larger 2.4 GiB index
/healthz was moved off :8080 in 3.8.0, so probes never connect

explanation.cause: Liveness probe gives up before the new startup path opens the HTTP port
explanation.why: 3.8.0 loads a 2.4 GiB index before listening on :8080, which takes ~45 s. Liveness starts at 20 s and tolerates three 10 s failures, so kubelet kills the container at ~41 s. Every restart begins the load from zero, so no pod ever finishes. A startupProbe would hold liveness off until the app is up.
explanation.tell: The loader is still making progress (87%) one second before the kill, the restart reason is the liveness probe rather than OOMKilled, and “connection refused” is a port that isn’t open yet.

alert.title: geo-router p99 latency 410ms over 150ms SLO for 10m

items.value: pods moved to node pool c-64 (64 vCPU, was 8 vCPU)

question: What is driving geo-router’s tail latency?
options: A 2-core CPU limit that is too low for steady-state load
Noisy neighbours on the 64-core nodes stealing CPU time
Cross-zone hops added by the new node pool’s placement
GOMAXPROCS=64 bursts burning the 2-core CFS quota early

explanation.cause: Go sized GOMAXPROCS to 64 host cores, so bursts exhaust the CFS quota
explanation.why: Before Go 1.25 the runtime ignores the cgroup limit and runs 64 Ps on a 64-core node. Bursts and GC fan out across dozens of threads and spend the 200 ms-per-100 ms quota in a few ms; the kernel then freezes the whole container until the period ends. Average CPU stays low while requests caught in a freeze wait.
explanation.tell: Throttled periods jumped from 3% to 60% while average CPU stayed at 36% of the limit and steal time is near zero — the cgroup quota, not the node, is stalling the process.

explanation.why: Every pod here had an ephemeral-storage request of 0, so all of them “exceeded” it and kubelet ranked them by priority first. evidence.label: edge-proxy CPU, mean of all PoPs

lines.text: ruleset waf-managed v8811 published: +1 rule (id 100412, action=simulate)
v8811 acked by 41/41 PoPs in 2.5s
worker 7: event loop blocked for 4210ms
502 returned: request not handled within 5000ms (worker saturated)
no attack signatures active; top client share 0.4% of requests
edge-proxy binary 2026.10.06-2 at 100% since Tue 10:14; no rollouts in progress

question: What took the edge down?
options: A WAF regex pushed to every PoP at once is burning CPU
A volumetric L7 attack saturating CPU in every PoP
The last edge-proxy binary has a CPU regression
An origin outage making edges hold requests and spin

explanation.cause: A new WAF rule with a backtracking regex reached every PoP within seconds
explanation.why: Rule data bypassed the staged rollout that binaries get, so one rule hit all 41 PoPs in 2.5 s. Its pattern includes .*(?:.*=.*), which backtracks catastrophically on ordinary requests. Simulate mode still runs the regex, so every request burned CPU until workers starved and the proxies returned 502s.
explanation.tell: CPU jumps to 100% in every PoP within seconds of the ruleset publish while request volume stays flat and the binary hasn’t changed in days — a global data push, not traffic or code.

question: Tap the line that explains why the 5.13.2 pods started failing.

explanation.cause: The migration dropped a column that the still-running old pods query
explanation.why: The drop ran as a pre-deploy Job, so it finished before any 5.14.0 pod existed. With maxUnavailable 0, all traffic was still on 5.13.2, which selects legacy_sku, and errors only drained as new pods replaced old ones. Drops belong in a later release (expand/contract), once no running code reads the column.
explanation.tell: The UndefinedColumn errors come from the old 6c9f7d8b5 ReplicaSet and start one second after alembic ran “drop orders.legacy_sku”. The QueuePool timeout is fallout, not cause.

question: Why did the canary pass?
options: The analysis failed open when its metrics query errored
The canary saw almost no traffic and none on the bad route
Promotion to 100% overloaded the DB with new pool connections
Canary pods ran stale config that happened to hide the bug

explanation.cause: At 2 a.m. a 5% canary got 41 requests, none on the only route 5.0.0 broke
explanation.why: Overnight traffic is ~40 req/min, so 5% for 20 minutes is a couple of requests a minute — and POST /v1/invoices never landed on the canary. “0 errors” was a sample of nothing. The analysis needed a minimum request count per critical route, or synthetic traffic, before it could pass.
explanation.tell: The verdict rests on 41 requests with zero on POST /v1/invoices, and post-promotion errors are fast (3–4 ms), deterministic, and only on that route — a code bug, not load.

question: Why are errors still at 18% after the rollback?
options: 2.8.4 has the same bug; the regression predates 2.9.0
Rollback hasn’t finished and 2.9.0 pods still take traffic
Rollback reverted the image but not the 200 ms timeout
ledger-svc degraded at 14:02 and is timing out calls

explanation.cause: rollout undo restored the pod template, not the ConfigMap shipped with it
explanation.why: Deployment revisions only track .spec.template. The ConfigMap edit landed in the same apply but lives outside the revision history, so rollout undo brought back the 2.8.4 image while every new pod still read LEDGER_TIMEOUT_MS=200 — below ledger-svc’s 310 ms p99.
explanation.tell: Every failure gives up at ~200 ms, matching the ConfigMap diff. ledger-svc’s p99 hasn’t moved and all 12 pods already run 2.8.4.

query-cache 1.9.1 rolled out to 6/6 pods
flag ranker-v2 updated by j.okafor: rollout 0% -> 100% (env=prod)
ranker-v2: feature lookup failed: rpc error: code = ResourceExhausted desc = quota exceeded for consumer search-api
evicted 1204 keys (maxmemory reached)
ranker-v2: feature lookup failed: rpc error: code = ResourceExhausted desc = quota exceeded for consumer search-api

question: What started the errors?
options: search-api 7.3.0 shipped a regression in the query path
feature-store is failing for every caller, not just search
query-cache 1.9.1 evicting hot keys and shifting load
Flipping ranker-v2 to 100% of prod traffic at 10:42:05

explanation.cause: Flag ranker-v2 jumped from 0% to 100%, sending every query down a new path
explanation.why: A flag flip is a production change with no deploy attached. ranker-v2 makes a feature-store call per query; at 100% that needed twice search-api’s per-consumer quota, so ResourceExhausted errors started 14 s after the flip. Ramping 1% → 10% → 50% would have hit the quota at a fraction of the blast radius.
explanation.tell: Errors start at 10:42, 87 minutes after the 7.3.0 rollout but seconds after the flag change, and every error carries the ranker-v2 prefix and a per-consumer quota.
